simple.meaning: נֵצֶר (nêtser) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a shoot ; figuratively, a descendant.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Isaiah 11:1. The surrounding context includes righteousness, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נֵצֶר (H5342) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: נֵצֶר (nêtser) / H5342 is traced through Isaiah 11:1, Isaiah 14:19, Isaiah 60:21, Daniel 11:7 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse,

timeline.evidenceText: A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse,

But you are cast away from your tomb like an abominable branch, clothed with the slain, who are thrust through with the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit; like a dead body trodden under foot.
Then your people will all be righteous.
“But out of a shoot from her roots one will stand up in his place, who will come to the army, and will enter into the fortress of the king of the north, and will deal against them, and will prevail.
